title: MWS 3-year resurvey — Behavioral
description: Diet, alcohol, and smoking behaviors reported at the 3-year resurvey.

F1FQORGN.title: Frequency of eating organic food
F1FQORGN.$comment: Source's own code list includes -1=Not on questionnaire for this field (not available on the 9903/9907 versions, available on 9909/0012) -- kept as the source-documented sentinel, same unenforced treatment as recruitment's REXANY (D020/D021): no skip pair added against F1QTYPE, the field's own -1 code covers it.

F15YDIET.title: Major diet changes in the last 5 years
F15YDIET.$comment: Available on every questionnaire version -- no not_on_questionnaire sentinel needed, generic missing_numeric fallback per D020.

F1ALCNUM.title: Alcoholic drinks per week
F1ALCNUM.$comment: Steward confirmed: non-drinkers were instructed to answer 0, so no skip rule applies -- 0 is a real, substantive value, not a sentinel. Real-count ceiling of 96 (rather than an arbitrary agent guess) follows directly from the source's own 97 code, whose description ('97+') implies any true count of 97 or more is captured by that code instead. 97 and 99 are the source's own two distinct 'unknown' codes (kept as their own const branches, not merged into missing_numeric, same treatment as F1MENOAG's 77/99 -- D051).

F1ALCEAT.title: Drinks alcohol with meals
F1ALCEAT.$comment: Steward confirmed this field is not skipped for non-drinkers (F1ALCNUM=0) in the real questionnaire, despite there being no explicit instruction either way -- some non-drinking participants may have left it blank on their own judgment, but nothing in the source documents a structural not-applicable case, so no skip rule is added and no not_applicable branch is included. Any gap here is generic missing_numeric.

F1ALCDAY.title: Number of drinking days per week
F1ALCDAY.$comment: Source states no explicit valid range, but the field's own 'per week' framing structurally caps it at 7 -- not a source-stated bound in the D/E columns, but not an arbitrary agent guess either. Steward confirmed this field is not skipped for non-drinkers -- no not_applicable branch, same as F1ALCEAT.

F1DRTEA.title: Tea consumption
F1DRTEA.$comment: Source states no valid range; 0-30 cups/day is an agent-decided plausibility ceiling, chosen well clear of the source's own 97/99 special codes to avoid collision. Same 97/99 treatment as F1ALCNUM.

F1DRCOF.title: Coffee consumption
F1DRCOF.$comment: Same structure and reasoning as F1DRTEA.

F1CIGSPD.title: Cigarettes per day
F1CIGSPD.x-universe: Participants who have ever smoked (F1SMOKE=2 Past or 3 Current) -- someone who has never smoked skips this and any other smoking-related follow-up questions.
F1CIGSPD.$comment: Corrects D060 (superseded): the real questionnaire's actual smoking-status question is 'have you ever been a smoker?' -- a Never answer skips this and subsequent smoking questions entirely, so this IS a real skip pattern, unlike recruitment's RCIGSPD/RSMOKE pair (D035 doesn't transplant here). Steward confirmed '1=None' stays as a real, untouched answer option for Past/Current smokers who report smoking zero on average -- not remapped to not_applicable. not_applicable branch enforced by a mother-file skip pair keyed on F1SMOKE -- D062.

F1SMOKE.title: Smoking status
F1SMOKE.$comment: Source marks this field 'Derived' for every questionnaire version. 3-level code list, distinct from recruitment's 4-level RSMOKE (which also had a separate 'Not current' level). Real skip pattern against F1CIGSPD -- D062 (corrects D060, which wrongly transplanted recruitment's D035 no-skip reasoning onto this field pair).
